title: Open extension scalar/site square on flat models
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes and let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings. Work in ordinary constant-ring module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $T=-\otimes_A^L B$ for derived change of rings along $A\to B$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $N=\nu^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $\delta:T N\cong N T$ for the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Let $t_j:Tj_{!,A}\cong j_{!,B}T$ be the sheaf tensor comparison, derived on K-flat models, induced by retaining each extension summand and tensoring its section with $b\in B$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]. Let $e_{j,R}:N_Xj_{!,R}^{\rm et}\cong j_{!,R}^{\rm pro}N_U$ be the canonical site comparison for $R=A,B$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison].
If $P$ is a bounded flat complex representing an etale object $L$, then $j_!P$ is flat termwise and K-flat on either site (on the pro-etale site use $N_UP$), and
$$j_{!,B}^{\rm pro}(\delta_{U,L})\circ t_j(N_UL)\circ T_X(e_{j,A}(L))=e_{j,B}(L_B)\circ N_X(t_j(L))\circ\delta_{X,j_{!,A}^{\rm et}L}.$$
These comparisons are natural in $L$. For composable open immersions $j_1,j_2$, their scalar comparisons satisfy $t_{j_2j_1}=j_{2!,B}(t_{j_1})\circ t_{j_2}(j_{1!,A}(-))$ after the canonical open compositors [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]; the site comparisons obey the corresponding composition identity. Identity opens give identity comparisons. Flatness and K-flatness use [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] [def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); proetale.tex Tag 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison). Agent comparison of these specified tensor and site maps.

proof.text: On either localized site, for a flat module sheaf $F$ on $U$ the tensor formula identifies $(-)\otimes_A j_!F$ with the composite $G\mapsto j_!(j^*G\otimes_A F)$. Restriction and extension by zero are exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and the middle functor is exact by flatness. Thus $j_!F$ is flat. The tensor identification is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]; the identifications of the small sites with their open localizations are part of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. This argument does not use geometric stalks of the pro-etale topos.

source.place: Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; exact localized restriction and extension, Tags 03DI and 03DJ

proof.text: A bounded flat $P$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The comparison pullback is exact and identifies the constant ring sheaves, by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] to $\nu_U$ with the constant-$A$ ring identification: $N_UP$ has flat terms and is K-flat. It has the same degree bounds since an additive functor sends zero to zero. Step 1 therefore gives flat terms for both $j^{et}_!P$ and $j^{pro}_!N_UP$; their unchanged bounds and the bounded-above flat lemma make both K-flat. In particular these complexes compute scalar extension by ordinary termwise tensor with $B$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], without assuming $B$ is $A$-flat.

First work with sheaves. Write $e=j^{et}_{!,A}$, $d=j^{pro}_{!,A}$, $C=N$, and $\rho_T:C_T(F\otimes_A G)\to C_TF\otimes_A C_TG$ for the ordinary tensorator. Identify $C_T(B_T)$ with $B_T$ using [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] at coefficient $B$ and the underlying-module construction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Thus $\delta_T=\rho_{T,-,B}^{-1}$. The maps $\kappa^e_{F,B}:e(F\otimes_A B_U)\to eF\otimes_A B_X$ and $\kappa^d$ in [lem-sf-open-comparison-tensor-normalization] are the inverses of the specified scalar comparisons: their open-adjunction transposes are the identity on each section over $U$, so their inverse sends the original tensor generator $s\otimes b$ to the extension generator with section $s\otimes b$. This follows directly from the summand prescription in [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] and the sheafification universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The site comparison $c$ in that lemma is precisely $e_{j,A}$, by [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization]. When $F$ already has a $B$-action, naturality of $c_F$ in its multiplication endomorphisms makes it $B$-linear; its open-unit equation is also the $B$-unit equation, so uniqueness of the open-adjunction transpose identifies it with $e_{j,B}$. All these identifications take place in module-sheaf categories.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison; agent specialization of the existing open-unit and tensor-normalization statements

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-open-comparison-tensor-normalization] with its coefficient ring equal to $A$, its first module equal to an arbitrary $F$, and its second module equal to the constant $A$-algebra sheaf $B_X$. Its restriction comparison $a_B:C_UB_U\to j_{pro}^*C_XB_X$ is the canonical identity on constant sections, so $h=(1\otimes a_B)\rho_U$ becomes $\rho_U$. The cited equation is
$$(c_F\otimes1)\rho_X C_X(\kappa^e)=\kappa^d\,d(\rho_U)\,c_{F\otimes_A B}.$$
Invert the two $\kappa$ maps and the two $\rho$ maps and rearrange this equality to obtain
$$d(\rho_U^{-1})\,(\kappa^d)^{-1}(c_F\otimes1)=c_{F\otimes_A B}\,C_X((\kappa^e)^{-1})\,\rho_X^{-1}.$$
By Step 3 these are exactly the two maps of the requested scalar/site square. Each map is $B$-linear: multiplication by $b'$ acts on $s\otimes b$ through $s\otimes b'b$, and every displayed comparison preserves that action. Equality of the underlying sheaf maps is equality of $B$-linear sheaf maps, since forgetting an ordinary module structure is faithful. No faithfulness assertion about derived restriction of scalars is being made.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison; agent algebraic rearrangement of the cited sheaf tensor compatibility equation

proof.text: Apply Step 4 to each $P^n$. Naturality of the sheaf comparisons makes these equalities commute with the differentials, so they give equal chain maps of $B$-module sheaves. By Step 2 all scalar extensions whose source must be resolved are computed on the indicated flat K-flat complexes. Exactness of $N$ and $j_!$ allows their comparisons to be applied degreewise even to $P\otimes_A B$. The canonical derived tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] is computed on those models; the etale scalar comparison is the one of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor], and the pro-etale tensor comparison is [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. Consequently the equal chain maps represent precisely the two composites in the statement, now in $D(X_{proet},B)$. The cited comparisons are natural, including [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]; hence their composites are natural in the derived object $L$, independently of its chosen bounded flat representative.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor, on the flat models from Step 2; proetale.tex Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison

proof.text: For $U\xrightarrow{j_1}V\xrightarrow{j_2}X$, use the canonical open compositor of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. On a section over an object mapping to $U$, its presheaf description simply composes the two factorizations and retains the section. This description follows from the extension prescription [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]: the compositor is the adjunct of the identity after the two restrictions. Both scalar-comparison routes therefore send a generator indexed by the two factorizations, tensored with $b$, to the generator indexed by their composite with section $s\otimes b$. On an object without the relevant factorization the source presheaf is zero. The tensor product and extension are sheafified presheaf constructions [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], so equality on these generators implies equality of the sheaf maps, including when an intermediate extension has already been sheafified, by applying the sheafification universal property at each stage. This proves the scalar composition identity. The computation with the unique identity factorization gives the identity scalar comparison. Apply this argument degreewise to flat K-flat models to obtain the displayed derived identity; Step 1 and the same tensor test show open extension preserves the flat terms used here.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 03DJ, localized extension construction; Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent computation on the generating sections

proof.text: For the site comparisons, composition compatibility is already part of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], with the open compositors of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. For an identity open, its open adjunction units and restriction comparison are identities; the normalization equation of [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization] then forces $c_{id}$ to be the identity. Exact degreewise extension preserves both equations in the derived categories. This supplies the site composition and identity clauses, with the same canonical comparisons as in Steps 3--5.
